rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify capabilities BEFORE asserting, not after.

The access-surface pass runs in-thread...') asserts a platform-mechanics fact I verified directly and found false: `content/skills/access-control-analysis/SKILL.md` frontmatter reads `context: fork` (line 4), identical to `content/skills/stride/SKILL.md` frontmatter (`context: fork`, line 4). The repo's own reference doc confirms what that field does: `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/claude-code-for-engineers.md` line 269 -- '`context: fork` | runs the skill in its own subagent context instead of inline' -- with no override path documented (personal vs. project skill, invocation phrasing, or exercise design does not change it). So access-control-analysis forks into a subagent exactly like stride does; M3 dispatches TWO subagents this way, not one, and this exercise's pass does not run in-thread. This file's own text elsewhere gets it right and now contradicts the new note: Push-back move P1 (L125, expanded L151) says 'let the skill run as a subagent,' and Leap Test #1 (L141/L167) says 'Invokes the access-control-analysis skill as a subagent.' Harm: a false in-thread/subagent-count claim in a maintainer block is exactly the kind of assertion a later editor or trainer reasons from (context-budget planning, or 'fixing' the leap-test/push-back lines to match L106's wrong claim instead of the reverse).
